title: ICGMM: CXL-enabled Memory Expansion with Intelligent Caching Using Gaussian Mixture Model
problem: CXL-enabled memory expansion systems suffer from substantial cache miss penalties and sub-optimal caching due to data access granularity mismatch between DRAM cache and SSD storage. Inefficient hardware cache management limits the effectiveness of these systems.
motivation: CXL creates a unified memory space for fast cache and slow storage expansion, but demands smarter cache policies to bridge the performance gap between computational speed and data communication rates.
method: Traditional cache management removes the least recently used data when space runs out, but this oversimplifies how real data is actually accessed. ICGMM instead uses a Gaussian Mixture Model (a statistical approach that identifies patterns in data) to learn which pieces are likely to be accessed next, then removes the least likely candidates when the cache fills up. The system is prototyped on an FPGA (field-programmable hardware chip), allowing engineers to test whether this learning-based policy works better in real hardware.
key_novelty: A Gaussian Mixture Model learns data access patterns to improve cache eviction decisions, outperforming traditional LRU eviction and more complex LSTM approaches while requiring less hardware to implement.
contributions: ICGMM: GMM-based cache management policy for CXL memory systems with hardware optimization
FPGA implementation demonstrating practical feasibility and 10,000x speedup over LSTM-based baselines
Cache miss rate reduction of 0.32% to 6.14% and SSD access latency reduction of 16.23% to 39.14% versus LRU
Efficient hardware design using fewer resources than LSTM-based alternatives
